jobs_results.description:
Widener University is currently seeking an AI Solutions Specialist. Reporting to the Vice President for Enrollment & Technology/Chief Information Officer, this newly created position will help the university's administrative units put artificial intelligence to practical use, improving the speed and quality of the work that supports our students, faculty, and staff. The role will report directly to the Vice President while it is being established, then move into the Information Technology department.

 This is a hands-on role. The AI Solutions Specialist will work with units such as Admissions, Student Financial Services, the Registrar, Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology Services, etc. to identify high-value opportunities, then personally configure, test, deploy, and monitor the tools that address them. It is also strategic: the position maintains a university-wide view of where AI is and should be used, recommends what the university should license, and builds the training that equips staff to leverage these new tools.

 Qualified candidates will have both technological expertise and the interpersonal skills necessary to engage colleagues and campus stakeholders. Much of this work involves understanding how staff actually do their jobs and earning the trust required to manage change. The university is interested in what demonstrably works, not in adopting technology for its own sake. Duties and priorities will shift on an ongoing basis, so the successful candidate will bring comfort with ambiguity, a willingness to "figure it out," and the autonomy to identify opportunities rather than wait for assignments.

 This position is eligible for regular remote/flex work, and the university will consider fully remote candidates; some on-campus presence may be expected during onboarding and periodically thereafter. Widener is committed to fostering an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive.

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (including, but not limited to): 

 Essential Duties: 

  Partner with administrative units to identify work that is repetitive, slow, error-prone, or backlogged, and assess honestly whether AI is the right tool.Configure, test, and deploy AI solutions hands-on: prompts, custom assistants and agents, document-grounded chat and search over a unit's own content, drafting and summarization workflows, and extraction of structured data from forms and correspondence.Connect AI capabilities to existing university systems using workflow automation tools so that outputs land where staff already work.Monitor deployed solutions on a regular basis reviewing output quality, tracking adoption, catching degradation, and adjusting configuration as content, processes, and vendor capabilities change. Document configurations, prompts, and known limitations so that deployments are supportable and repeatable.Define and report success measures for each deployment (time saved, turnaround time, error rates, volume handled) and recommend retiring or rebuilding what does not deliver.In partnership with others, design and deliver practical training workshops, office hours, and role-specific guides that raises baseline AI fluency and builds capable practitioners in business units.Evaluate new tools, assess vendor claims critically, maintain a roadmap of AI use across administrative units, and report progress and priorities to university leadership.Ensure that every deployment adheres to university policy and applicable requirements for data security and privacy, record retention, and appropriate use.  Secondary Responsibilities:

  Serve on division and campus-wide committees and participate in process improvement projects or strategic initiatives as assigned.Keep informed about developments in artificial intelligence, automation, and higher education technology, including relevant policies, regulations, and state and federal laws.Potential for modest supervisory responsibilities and/or collaboration opportunities with student employees or interns.Perform other job-related duties as assigned or directed to support departmental needs and align with the mission, values and goals of Enrollment & Technology and Widener University.  MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS (education/training and experience required):

 Required:

  Bachelor's degree.Demonstrated hands-on experience building solutions with current generative AI tools (e.g., configuring custom assistants or agents, developing prompts for production use, or deploying document-grounded chat or retrieval over an organization's own content).Working knowledge of at least one major enterprise AI platform (for example, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Google Gemini, ChatGPT Enterprise, or Anthropic Claude), including its administrative settings.Comfort working with data in spreadsheets and structured files, and an understanding of how systems exchange data through APIs.Ability to evaluate AI output critically recognizing hallucination, bias, and quiet failure and to build the checks that catch problems before end users do.Demonstrated ability to map a business process, identify where the friction actually lies, and design a change that staff will adopt.Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, written and verbal, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical colleagues clearly and without condescension.Customer service orientation and ability to interact with a wide variety of individuals within a complex and dynamic environment.Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with thoroughness and attention to detail.Ability to work independently, manage multiple projects, and prioritize among competing needs.Ability to identify gaps in one's own knowledge and locate the resources to learn on one's own, essential in a field changing this quickly.  Formal software development experience is not required; candidates who have built practical solutions through configuration rather than code are encouraged to apply.

 Preferred:

  Master's degree.Experience in higher education, or in another complex, decentralized organization.Experience delivering training or change management to non-technical staff.Familiarity with enterprise administrative systems such as Ellucian Colleague, Technolutions Slate, etc.Scripting ability (e.g., Python or JavaScript).  SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

  Occasional travel to the university's campuses will be required.This position may require vacation restrictions during times of peak activity in the department.The employee must have the ability to occasionally lift/or move 10+ pounds.The employee will perform repetitive motion using computer mouse and keyboard to type.  Qualified candidates must submit resume and cover letter for consideration. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Only those selected to interview will be contacted.

 All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Widener University is committed to fostering an inclusive community in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing equal educational and employment opportunities for all persons without regard to age, color, national origin, race, religion, disability, veteran status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or status as a protected veteran.

Dynamic teaching, active scholarship, personal attention and experiential learning are key components of the Widener Experience. Located in Chester, PA, Widener's main campus is nestled between Philadelphia, PA and Wilmington, DE, with Law Schools located in both Harrisburg and Wilmington. jobs_results.description:
Summary The AI Specialist is an individual-contributor role accountable for the end-to-end design, development, deployment and lifecycle performance of secure, reliable and responsible artificial intelligence solutions that deliver measurable business value, better decision-making, automation and digital transformation across Pharming. The role translates prioritized business outcomes, enterprise AI direction and architectural standards into production-ready AI, machine-learning and generative-AI capabilities that can be adopted sustainably across global functions.


Reporting to the Head of AI, Data & Analytics, the AI Specialist works with high autonomy and serves as technical authority for assigned AI products and initiatives. The role leads complex cross-functional delivery, makes delegated technical decisions, assures engineering and responsible-AI quality, guides colleagues and partners, and coordinates with business, data, architecture and control stakeholders to deliver valuable, secure and supportable solutions.


This is a hybrid role based in our Warren, NJ office with an expectation of 2-3 in office days in office each week and the flexibility to adjust schedules depending on business needs.


What you'd do
AI solution design and delivery


Own the technical design, development, testing, deployment and transition to support of complex AI, machine-learning and generative-AI solutions that address prioritized business outcomes and operate reliably in production


Translate prioritized use cases into solution designs and delivery plans; challenge feasibility and data readiness and select model, retrieval, agent, automation and integration patterns based on value, risk and maintainability.


Design and maintain reusable AI components, services, reference implementations and engineering patterns that accelerate delivery, reduce duplication and improve consistency across Pharming.


Define solution-level quality and evaluation criteria and engineer for reliability through automated testing, monitoring, observability, error handling, performance management, documentation and operational support practices.


Lead application of modern software-engineering and AI lifecycle practices, including version control, code review, CI/CD, model and prompt versioning, deployment automation, reproducible experimentation and controlled release management.


Drive resolution of data, platform and integration dependencies with data engineering and platform teams so assigned AI solutions use trusted, governed data and progress from experimentation to sustainable production use


Responsible AI, governance and lifecycle


Apply responsible-AI standards and define solution-specific controls, human oversight and technical guardrails proportionate to intended use and risk.


Lead solution-level AI risk assessment with business owners, governance stakeholders and control functions, translating risk classification, intended use, quality expectations and governance requirements into enforceable technical controls and evidence.


Embed privacy, cybersecurity, access control, data protection, retention and compliance requirements into solution architecture and deployment and assure that required control evidence is complete before release.


Establish and maintain traceability across models, prompts, data sources, configurations, evaluations, approvals and releases so solutions can be reviewed, monitored, audited and changed in a controlled manner.


Own lifecycle monitoring for assigned solutions, including performance, reliability, drift, quality and relevant risk indicators, and lead timely technical remediation when results or controls fall outside agreed tolerances.


Lead the technical delivery and documentation of regulated and GxP-relevant AI use cases where applicable, working with Quality and validation stakeholders to meet Pharming's quality, validation and regulatory requirements.


Technical leadership and transformation
Provide hands-on leadership for complex AI initiatives, set implementation direction, assure adherence to standards, and make risks, trade-offs and exceptions visible to decision-makers.


Partner with business, product, data and analytics owners to define value and success measures, convert high-value opportunities into usable solutions, and lead transition from proof-of-concept to sustainable production.


Coordinate technical dependencies with Data Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Enterprise Applications and Global IT Operations & Service Delivery so assigned solutions align with data, integration, cloud, infrastructure, security and service-management requirements.


Lead evidence-based assessment of AI technologies, models, platforms and vendors and recommend fit-for-purpose choices based on value, scalability, risk, interoperability and lifecycle impact.


Raise team capability through design reviews, mentoring, documentation, AI literacy and communities of practice, sharing reusable knowledge across internal teams and partners.


Perform other duties as assigned.


What you'd need
Relevant bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience.


At least four years of progressive experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, software engineering or related disciplines, including substantial hands-on ownership of complex production AI or machine-learning solutions.


Proven track record designing, deploying and operating multiple AI or machine-learning solutions in complex or global environments; regulated-industry experience is strongly preferred.


Advanced practical experience with modern AI and machine-learning approaches, including generative AI, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, model evaluation, agentic or automation patterns and cloud-based AI services where relevant.


Demonstrated ownership of production AI lifecycle practices, including testing, CI/CD, model and prompt versioning, observability, controlled deployment and remediation; MLOps or LLMOps experience is preferred.


Advanced programming skills, particularly Python or an equivalent language used for AI and machine-learning development, together with strong software-engineering, API, integration, code-review and maintainability practices.


Strong understanding of responsible AI, model risk, privacy, cybersecurity, data governance, explainability and access-control principles, with demonstrated ability to translate governance and regulatory requirements into technical controls and evidence.


Ability to lead complex workstreams through expertise and influence, decide under ambiguity, communicate trade-offs to stakeholders, mentor colleagues and resolve cross-functional challenges with limited supervision.


Fluent English required; ability to collaborate effectively across global teams and time zones.


Commitment and alignment to Pharming's mission, core values and behaviors.


Who we are
We’re built on a simple belief: people living with rare diseases deserve more. Pharming is a global biotechnology company taking on some of the toughest rare disease challenges. We develop and commercialize innovative therapies for rare and ultra-rare immunological and genetic diseases with significant unmet need, where our scientific and commercial expertise, long-term commitment, and real partnership can help advance care.


We put patients at the heart of our work. Their insights, along with those of caregivers, clinicians, scientists, and parters, shape our strategy, guide our decisions, and help turn science into meaningful progress. We keep it simple, act with urgency, and get it done – expanding access to approved therapies, advancing high-value pipeline programs, and building a leading global rare disease company.


Our vision is simple: a world where people living with rare diseases don’t wait for progress or care. Together with the communities who inspire us, we’re opening new possibilities – proving that breakthroughs aren’t just discovered. They’re created together.


Ready to make a difference? Join us.


What it’s like to work here


At Pharming, every role helps move rare disease therapies closer to the people who need them. We make it happen together, across teams, disciplines, and borders, because breakthroughs don’t happen in silos. Rare diseases are complex, and meaningful progress takes people who ask better questions, challenge each other, and turn insight into action.


Here, you won’t work on the sidelines. Pharming is a place for builders, problem-solvers, and bold thinkers who move with urgency, take ownership, and stay focused on what matters most: improving the lives of people living with rare diseases. Advancing rare disease care isn’t the work of one team or one leader.


It’s all of us, building what’s next together.


This is also an important moment of transformation for Pharming’s digital and technology capabilities, as they evolve from a traditional support function into a more integrated, enterprise-wide enabler of business value. You will have the opportunity to influence how applications, data, technology, processes, and ways of working develop across the organization, helping to build scalable, resilient, and future-ready capabilities that support Pharming’s continued growth.


Salary range
Pharming takes into consideration a combination of candidate’s work experience, training, and education, as well as the scope of the role, complexity, and external market and internal value when determining a salary level.


The base salary range for this job is from $115,000 to $155,000 per year.
